Segment 6 says the Recipient will not disclose the Confidential Information to any third party, with no carve-out for consultants, agents or advisors. That is incompatible with the statement that sharing with third parties is permitted.
Segment 3 bars disclosure to any third party, and the clauses do not say whether employees are included, so the segments neither permit nor bar sharing with the Recipient employees.

Segment 15 lets the Receiving Party develop, acquire or market products or services similar to the Disclosing Party products, but it does not speak to acquiring information from a third party. The statement is therefore not addressed in substance.
Possible risk: no injunctive or equitable relief for a breach of confidence.

The NDA has no general purpose limit on use, but segment 30 lets the Receiving Party use information retained in its personnel unaided memory for any purpose, a carve-out that is incompatible with an absolute use restriction on the same matter.
The segments cover use, confidentiality and the fact of negotiations, but none addresses reverse engineering of objects embodying Confidential Information.

Paragraph 'Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict' lets the Receiving Party use information retained in unaided memory for any purpose, which is a grant of a right to Confidential Information and so is incompatible with the statement.
The segments set the obligations to expire at the earlier of three years after signing or completion of the Sale, but they do not say whether obligations survive termination of the Agreement.

Segment 28 expressly limits Confidential Information to technical information and excludes business or financial information, which matches the statement. However, segments 6 and 7 define Confidential Information much more broadly, so the NDA is internally inconsistent and the label is uncertain.

The only nearby text is the residuals clause in segment 30, which covers use of information kept in unaided memory, not acquiring similar information from a third party. The segments do not address third-party acquisition either way.
Clause 'In the event of any breach' requires the breaching party to pay a fixed sum of US$500,000 as a penalty irrespective of actual loss, which is a fixed penalty for breach.

The shown segments cover use limits, copies and survival but contain no duty to notify the Disclosing Party promptly of unauthorized use or disclosure. Segment 22 covers responsibility for breaches, not notice.

Segment 22 makes each Party liable for breaches by its employees, which presupposes employee access but does not expressly permit sharing with them. Segment 19 bars disclosure to third parties without approval, and employees are not named either way, so the segments do not clearly state the permission.
